modules.name: Power dialer
modules.description: Automatically dial the next contact when a call ends. Reps can skip, pause, reschedule or switch to manual dialing.

modules.name: Auto dialer
modules.description: Set the dialing speed, line ratio and campaign in one screen. Answering-machine detection helps reps focus on live conversations.

modules.name: Manual (preview) dialer
modules.description: Review the contact before calling, then log the outcome in one click. Keyboard shortcuts cover dialing and voicemail.

modules.name: Local presence
modules.description: Choose caller IDs from number pools that match the contact’s area code.

modules.name: Voicemail drop
modules.description: Use a saved voicemail message instead of repeating the same recording. Campaigns can have several templates.

modules.name: Inbound and IVR
modules.description: Build an IVR menu and route calls by rep, team, skill or opening hours. Queues show wait times, with overflow to voicemail or a backup team.

modules.name: AI Agent Caller (early access)
modules.description: An early-access voice agent is designed to qualify new leads, book through Calendly or GHL, and hand off a summary and lead score. The reported response target is 60 seconds, 24/7.

modules.name: SMS
modules.description: Manage two-way texts in a shared inbox. Use templates, send a text after a missed call and call directly from a thread.

modules.name: WhatsApp
modules.description: Use the WhatsApp Business API with a business number. Share files and images, and trigger follow-ups from call outcomes.

modules.name: Call recording
modules.description: Find useful moments in recordings and transcripts with keyword search. Build coaching playlists and use recording-consent controls.

modules.name: Live coaching
modules.description: Support reps on live calls with listen, whisper and barge modes, alongside a view of the call floor.

modules.name: Analytics
modules.description: Follow team activity, connect rates and talk time. Compare scripts, review the leaderboard and export weekly reports.

modules.name: Compliance
modules.description: Bring DNC checks, regional calling windows, consent records and exportable reports into the calling workflow.

modules.name: Enterprise controls
modules.description: Manage access with SSO/SAML, Okta, role permissions and audit logs. Separate teams through regional or departmental sub-accounts.

steps.title: Create an account
steps.description: Everything runs in Chrome over WebRTC, so there is no softphone or hardware to install.

steps.title: Connect the CRM
steps.description: About 2 minutes for GoHighLevel or Pipedrive.

steps.title: Map fields
steps.description: Match CRM fields to Voxiq contact fields so outcomes and notes sync back.

steps.title: Invite reps
steps.description: Assign seats, roles and phone numbers.

steps.title: Launch the dialer
steps.description: Load a list from a CSV file or a CRM view, set the dial ratio, local presence pool and voicemail, and start.

industries.name: Sales teams
industries.scenario: An inside sales team of 10 account executives works inbound leads and an outbound list from GoHighLevel. Reps dial by hand, and the manager learns about a bad call only when a deal is lost.
steps: The manager builds an outbound campaign from a GHL pipeline stage, with local presence and two voicemail templates.
Reps run the power dialer; answering machine detection skips voicemails and drops the template automatically.
Each call outcome is logged with one click, updating the GHL deal stage and firing follow-up workflows.
Inbound calls route round-robin to available reps, with the caller's deal history on screen before they answer.
The manager watches the live call floor, whispers to reps on key calls, and builds coaching playlists from recordings.
industries.features: power dialer, local presence, voicemail drop, GHL two-way sync, live coaching, rep leaderboard.
industries.measures: dials per rep per day, connect rate, meetings booked, pipeline created per rep.
industries.plan: Calls – Growth ($40) for recordings and advanced analytics.

industries.name: SDR / BDR teams
industries.scenario: An SDR team prospects cold lists all day to book meetings for account executives. Volume is the job, but most dials hit voicemail and answer rates on out-of-area numbers are low.
steps: Lists are loaded from CSV or a CRM view into an auto-dialer campaign with a 2:1 dial ratio.
Answering machine detection screens out voicemails in under a second, so SDRs only hear live people.
Local presence shows a caller ID matching each prospect's area code.
When a call goes unanswered, a WhatsApp or SMS intro follows automatically (Voxiq's example: wait 10 minutes, then send the intro template).
Booked meetings land in Calendly or the GHL calendar; recordings are searched by objection or competitor name to sharpen the script.
Script A/B tests show which opener converts better.
industries.features: auto dialer with AMD, dial ratio, local presence, multichannel follow-up, transcript search, script A/B testing.
industries.measures: live conversations per hour, connect rate by hour and area code, meetings booked per SDR.
industries.plan: Calls – Growth ($40) plus the SMS add-on ($70) for sequenced follow-ups.

industries.name: Small business
industries.scenario: A local service business with an owner and two staff answers calls between jobs. Missed calls go to a personal voicemail and many are never returned, so leads call the next business on the list.
steps: The business gets a Voxiq number and a simple IVR ("Press 1 for bookings, 2 for billing").
During business hours calls ring the team; after hours they go to voicemail.
Every missed call triggers an automatic text-back, so the caller hears from the business within moments.
Voicemails are transcribed and emailed to the owner.
The owner returns calls and texts from one inbox in the browser, with no desk phone.
industries.features: missed-call text-back, voicemail transcripts by email, business-hours routing, shared SMS inbox, browser calling.
industries.measures: missed calls returned within the hour, inbound leads converted to bookings.
industries.plan: Calls – Starter ($20) plus the SMS add-on ($70), since Starter alone excludes text-back.

industries.name: Enterprise
industries.scenario: A multi-region sales organization runs hundreds of reps across several departments. IT needs single sign-on and audit trails, legal needs consistent calling rules, and leadership wants one view across regions.
steps: IT connects SSO/SAML through Okta and sets custom permission tiers by role.
Each region or department gets a sub-account; phone numbers and compliance rules are managed centrally.
DNC checks, state calling hours and consent logging run before every dial, and compliance reports are exported for audit.
Leadership uses company-wide reporting and weekly PDF reports; audit logs record admin changes.
The REST API connects Voxiq to internal systems such as a data warehouse or a non-GHL CRM.
A dedicated customer success manager and an enterprise SLA cover rollout and support.
industries.features: SSO and Okta, role-based access, audit logs, sub-accounts, central compliance, REST API, AI call insights.
industries.measures: adoption per region, compliance exceptions, pipeline created per seat, cost per seat vs the legacy dialer.
industries.plan: Calls – Scale ($70) with an enterprise agreement.

industries.name: Real estate
industries.scenario: A brokerage's agents work a geographic farm list, expired and FSBO listings, and portal leads from sources such as Zillow. Portal leads go to whichever agent calls first, so a slow callback loses the deal.
steps: The whole farm list is loaded into a power-dialer campaign with local presence for the farm's area code.
New portal leads trigger the AI agent, which calls within 60 seconds, asks about timeline, budget and pre-approval, and books a showing on the agent's GHL calendar.
Warm leads hand off to the agent with a call summary and lead score; cold leads enter a nurture sequence.
Brochures, listing photos and comparables go out by WhatsApp from the business number.
Past clients are called on anniversaries for referrals, with outcomes logged in GHL.
industries.features: power dialer for farm lists, AI agent speed-to-lead, local presence, WhatsApp media, GHL calendar booking.
industries.measures: time to first call on portal leads, appointments set per agent, listings won from the farm.
industries.plan: Calls – Growth ($40) plus SMS ($70); add the AI agent when it leaves early access.

industries.name: Insurance
industries.scenario: An insurance agency sells new policies from purchased leads and must retain existing customers at renewal. Calling across states brings TCPA, calling-hour and recording-consent rules that vary by state.
steps: Renewal campaigns are segmented by policy expiry date (for example, 60, 30 and 7 days out) and dialed in turn.
Every number is checked against DNC lists, and calls are blocked outside each state's permitted hours.
Consent is logged with a timestamp, and recordings follow each state's consent rules.
Agents see the policy holder's history before dialing in preview mode, which suits higher-value renewals.
Unanswered renewal calls get an SMS or WhatsApp reminder; quotes and policy documents go out as attachments.
Compliance reports are exported for carrier or regulator audits.
industries.features: expiry-date segmentation, TCPA and DNC checks, state calling hours, consent logging, recording, preview dialer.
industries.measures: renewal retention rate, contacts reached before expiry, compliance exceptions.
industries.plan: Calls – Growth ($40) for recordings, plus SMS ($70).

industries.name: SaaS
industries.scenario: A SaaS company gets free-trial sign-ups and demo requests around the clock. Trials that nobody contacts in the first days rarely convert, and the sales team can't cover every time zone.
steps: A new sign-up triggers the AI agent within 60 seconds. It asks which CRM the prospect uses and how big their team is, then books a demo through Calendly.
Qualified leads reach an account executive with a summary and lead score in Slack or the CRM.
SDRs call trial users who haven't activated, from a CRM view filtered by trial day.
Transcripts are searched for competitor names and pricing objections to feed product and marketing.
Call outcomes update Pipedrive or GHL deal stages; Zapier pushes call events to product analytics or a spreadsheet.
industries.features: AI agent for 24/7 speed-to-lead, Calendly booking, Slack summaries, transcript search, Pipedrive and Zapier.
industries.measures: time to first touch on sign-ups, trial-to-demo rate, trial-to-paid conversion.
industries.plan: Calls – Scale ($70) for AI call insights.

industries.name: Collections
industries.scenario: A collections agency works large account queues where most calls go unanswered. Every contact must fall inside FDCPA call windows, and recordings are needed to defend disputes.
steps: Accounts are loaded into an auto-dialer campaign; Voxiq cites 300–400 accounts worked per collector per day.
FDCPA call windows and state calling hours are enforced before every dial, with DNC checks.
Answering machine detection skips voicemail; a compliant voicemail template is dropped instead.
Debtors who call back are routed by IVR to the collector who owns the account, with the account history on screen.
Every call is recorded and transcribed, so disputes are resolved by searching the transcript.
Payment reminders follow by SMS after unanswered calls, and outcomes such as promise-to-pay are logged with one click.
industries.features: FDCPA windows, auto dialer with AMD, call recording and transcript search, skill-based inbound routing, compliance reports.
industries.measures: right-party contacts per hour, promises to pay, dollars collected per collector, compliance exceptions.
industries.plan: Calls – Growth ($40) for recordings, plus SMS ($70).

industries.name: GoHighLevel agencies
industries.scenario: A marketing agency runs GoHighLevel for 10 local-business clients. Clients get leads from the agency's campaigns but don't call them fast enough, and the agency wants a new recurring revenue line.
steps: The agency white-labels Voxiq with its own name, logo and domain (for example, dialer.myagency.com).
Each client gets a sub-account with its own workspace and billing, managed from one agency dashboard.
Inside each client's GHL, a workflow action starts an AI outbound call when a new lead arrives, and booked appointments land on the client's GHL calendar.
Call outcomes move GHL pipeline stages and trigger the client's existing follow-up workflows.
The agency resells seats with margin; Voxiq's example is $49 wholesale against $149 resale per seat.
industries.features: white-label branding, client sub-accounts, native GHL workflow actions, AI agent, agency dashboard.
industries.measures: client lead-to-appointment rate, seats per client, agency margin per seat, client retention.
industries.plan: Agency Growth tier (up to 25 clients), priced on request.
industries.economics: Suggested resale is $97–197 per seat, which Voxiq puts at $5,000–10,000 in monthly recurring revenue for 10 clients with 5 seats each.
